chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, who said:

I used to go to Ibn Abi Layla regarding inheritance cases, and he would dispute/delay with me. When that prolonged for me, I complained about him to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) ordered the return of the restrained (property/heir) and the execution of inheritances? He said: So I went to him, and he did as he used to do. I said to him: I complained about you to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and he said to me such-and-such. Then Ibn Abi Layla made me swear that he said that to me, so I swore to him, and he ruled in my favor regarding that.

key_terms.الْحَبِيس: The restrained (one who is withheld from his inheritance or property)
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَدِّ الْحَبِيس: Returning the restrained (restoring the heir to their share)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on 'al-habīs' (the restrained heir/property) in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar* highlights the legal authority of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) in resolving inheritance disputes by invoking the Prophet's command to expedite the distribution of 'al-habīs' (restrained or withheld assets). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preventing the unjust delay of inheritances, a principle that distinguishes it from the practices of contemporary jurists like Ibn Abi Layla. The narrative illustrates the practical application of prophetic traditions in ensuring the swift transfer of wealth to rightful heirs.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Muhammed bin Khalid al-Barqi, from Abdullah bin Mughaira, from Abdul-Rahman al-Ju’fi, that he said:

I used to attend at Ibn Abi Layla with regards to inheritance, and he used to push me. When that had (lasted for a) prolonged (time), I complained about him to Ja’far ibn Muhammed, peace be upon them both, so he said: Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, ordered for the return of the restrained and the fulfilment of inheritance? He said: Then I went to him, and he did what he used to do, so I said to him: I complained about you to Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both, and he said to me such-and-such. Then Ibn Abi Layla made me swear that he said that, so I swore to him, and he ruled to my favor in that (case).
